subject: literature
passage: Anton Chekhov insisted that The Cherry Orchard (1904) was a comedy, "in places even a farce," and he was dismayed when Konstantin Stanislavski's company in Moscow staged it as a solemn tragedy about a family losing its estate. Critic Jonas Hallgrímsson sides with the playwright. The family ignores every warning that the orchard will be sold, the servants are clowns, and the characters' self-absorption is laughable rather than pitiable. Played straight, the play loses the irony that gives it life.
passage_b: An author's label for a play need not bind its audiences, and in this case comedy and grief are not rivals. The final act gives us the sound of axes already at work in the orchard and the old servant Firs, forgotten, lying down in the locked and empty house. Audiences laugh at these people and then find that the loss is real anyway. The play's power lies in its refusal to settle the matter, and a production that chooses either comedy or tragedy alone throws half of it away.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim that Chekhov was right in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that the family's self-absorption makes the play purely comic
choices.B: By denying that Chekhov ever described the play as a comedy
choices.C: By insisting that Stanislavski's tragic staging was the only correct interpretation
choices.D: By arguing that the play's comic and tragic elements coexist rather than one canceling the other

explanation.why: Hallgrímsson sides with Chekhov in calling the play a comedy. Text 2 says "comedy and grief are not rivals," points to the axes and the forgotten Firs, and argues that the play "refuses to settle the matter," so that a production choosing "either comedy or tragedy alone throws half of it away." The author of Text 2 would say Chekhov's label captures only part of the play.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says the loss "is real anyway" and that the play is not purely one thing.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 accepts that the author gave the play a label; it argues only that the label need not bind audiences.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says a production choosing tragedy alone, like one choosing comedy alone, loses half the play.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 argues that laughter and genuine loss coexist in the play.
